source_text: . At ego illam virtutem numquam dixi esse, sed vitium. Quod si non movetur concupiscendo, quid est quod adversus eam castitas dimicat continendo? Ubi sunt illa quae adversus eam confessus es exerceri sanctorum Hunc itaque motum ideo indecentem, quia inoboedientem, cum illi primi homines in sua carne sensissent, et in sua nuditate erubuissent, foliis ficulneis eadem membra texerunt: ut saltem arbitrio verecundantium velaretur, quod non arbitrio volentium movebatur; et quoniam pudebat quod indecenter libebat, operiendo fieret quod decebat
pass_a_gloss: . but ego that virtue never dixi to-be, but vice. that/which if not movetur concupiscendo, what is that/which adversus her chastity dimicat continendo? where are that which adversus her confessus es exerceri sanctorum this and-so movement for-that-reason indecentem, because inoboedientem, when/with illi primi human-beings in his-own in-flesh sensissent, and in his-own nuditate erubuissent, foliis ficulneis the-same members texerunt: so-that/as saltem by-decision verecundantium velaretur, that/which not by-decision volentium movebatur; and quoniam pudebat that/which indecenter libebat, operiendo fieret that/which decebat.

lemmas.lexica: LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium

pass_b_english: Augustine reports Julian interpreted his claim that desire is ‘indecent because disobedient’ as meaning that desire ‘is subject neither to body nor mind, but remains always untamed through a savage force.’

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
